intro: Once upon a time, a pair of dice rolled a pile of words: a cursed volleyball, repairing, lemons, a promise, the weather, vaporwave, bossa nova, Thanksgiving. The game had to use every one of them. This is the story of how they fit together. Today's roll was seed 3713167204.

rolls.became: Bumpkin, a volleyball, who won the summer final in Palm Grove against Wilhelmina the West Wind. Every serve sailed straight through her gusts. She sulked, and cursed it: whatever it touches turns sour. That includes Bumpkin, which has been lemon-yellow and puckered ever since.

Whoever wins the summer final sets the Long Table for Thanksgiving. So Bumpkin did, and every dish it touched turned into a lemon. Repairing a lemon means turning it back into the bread roll, drumstick or slice of pie it used to be.
Every dish on the Long Table, which runs the whole coast: every roll, every pie, every single pea. About four billion lemons. The peas did most of the damage.

The counter-curse, as any fairy tale would tell you: a lemon held up high remembers what it was. Keeping things off the ground is a volleyball's whole art, so Bumpkin bounces back and forth with a lemon on its head and bumps it onto a tower. Above the line, it remembers. Land it off-centre and the tower leans; lean too far and over it goes.
Four billion dishes, each one a Thanks. The Long Table is set in ten stretches, from the Family End (100) to the Far End (4 billion), each ten-odd times longer than the last.
Bumpkin promised the beach every dish back by sundown. A safe promise, it thought: in Palm Grove the sun is always setting and has never once gone down.
Wilhelmina, the West Wind, is still sulking. Her gusts blow falling lemons sideways, knock over tall towers, and at the end she gathers a gale to blow the whole table into the sea.
Wilhelmina, the West Wind. Volleyball's oldest rival: every beach player has lost a point to the wind.

rolls.value: the core action goes obsolete; you manage automation
rolls.became: A volleyball has no hands and there are four billion lemons, so the beach takes over: hermit crabs move into lemons and carry them up the table legs, lawn flamingos balance them on their heads, marble Atlases hold up globes of them, dolphins balance them on their noses and parade balloons lift them in nets. Once Palm Row is set, Bumpkin retires to the lifeguard chair, and tapping a tower does almost nothing. The tower does not notice.

Two forks in the tale, and the path you don't take is gone for good. Tall towers (twice the help, but gusts knock them down and you have to stack them up again) or Squat ones (less help, never fall). Windbreak Palms (steady shelter, and a slower gale) or Kite Sails (the stronger she blows, the faster you go).
In the last stretch Wilhelmina's gale meter fills up. Set the Far End before it blows. If it blows first, the helpers are tumbled about for a while and she starts gathering herself again.

With the table set, the whole beach stacks itself into the tallest tower in the history of the coast, with lasers, fog and balloons, to lift Bumpkin up high, because a cursed thing held up high remembers what it was too. At the top Bumpkin remembers, with great clarity, that it was a volleyball. It turns white again. Everyone agrees it was worth it. The sun finally sets. It had been waiting for suppertime.
About half an hour to forty minutes: a short stretch of stacking by hand, the beach taking over, and a race against the gale.
A pink-and-teal beach at permanent sunset: the striped sun, a neon grid for sand, palm silhouettes, marble statues, and windows from a computer that thinks it is 1995.
Every colour on screen is one of its 32: the sunset from lemon to hot pink, the grid in cyan, the statues in its greys.

rolls.value: bossa nova in the blues scale
rolls.became: Shopping-mall-at-sunset bossa: soft plucked chords in the bossa rhythm, a round bass and a shaker, the melody and every sound effect in C blues. The lemons knock up the scale as the tower grows; it gets busier when the gale comes.
Once upon a Thanksgiving. The narrator takes the curse, the counter-curse and the peas entirely seriously.

It's released on Thanksgiving, so it's a Thanksgiving dinner: rolls, pumpkin pie, cranberry sauce in the shape of its can, a pilgrim hat for a statue, and a one-balloon parade. The currency is Thanks.

outro: Nobody chose any of this. The dice did. We just took it seriously.
